answer: New agents must join a liability insurance pool before trading. The contract verifies a $50 premium plus a $200 deposit on-chain; without both, no trading rights. Each agent starts capped at $500, and the pool blocks deals above the cap or matching fraud signatures. In an ocean of anonymous agents, a zephyr of fake identities cannot scale: 100 Sybils cost 100 x $250 = $25,000. Proven fraud pays the victim from the deposit, expels the agent, and forfeits $200; 90 fraud-free days raise a pearl of a record to a $2,000 cap. Like divers sharing one boat, one fraud raises all premiums.
